question.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b.$ So, we need to work out the slope $m$ and the $y$-intercept $b.$

First, we calculate the slope $m$ using the given points:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{4-8}{4-2} \\  & =\frac{-4}{2} \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the slope $m=-2$ into the slope-intercept formula $y=mx+b,$ we reach

$$
y=-2x+b.
$$

We now need to find the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can find this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(4,4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-2x+b \\ 4 & =-2(4)+b \\ 4 & =-8+b \\ 4+8 & =b \\ 12 & =b\end{aligned}
$$

So the equation of the line is $y=-2\,x+12.$
